children: Asian chip shares extended their gains on sustained investor interest in AI trade.

South Korea's Kospi index was up 1%, helped by gains in both its chip giants -- Samsung Electronics Co and SK Hynix. The rise comes post the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) increased 1.3% in New York. The MSCI Asia Pacific index was up 0.4% with the IT sector contributing the most.
Brent increased 1.6% to $99.5 a barrel, its highest level since July. Crude prices climbed after the US attacked Iranian tankers near the Kharg Island crude export hub.

With the US-Iran war being in the seventh month, new attacks on energy infrastructure risk keeping oil rates elevated and complicate the outlook for interest rates and inflation. While the US says it has largely moved its attention towards putting economic pressure on Iran, repeated violence outbreaks keep the conflict simmering.

On another note, the yen strengthened for the third day in a row after US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said he has 'good insight' regarding what the Bank of Japan would do with its currency. The yen was up 0.4% to 153.31 per dollar, meanwhile Bloomberg's dollar gauge slipped 0.1%.

title: Asian chip shares gain, Kospi rises 1%; Brent rises towards $100
